==English==

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*sed-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|sete}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sǣte}}, possibly from (or simply cognate with) {{der|en|non|sæti|t=seat}}, both from {{der|en|gem-pro|*sētiją|t=seat}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*sed-|t=to sit}}; compare {{cog|ang|set|t=seat}}.

{{senseno|en|site|uc=1}} (“location or site”) is probably derived from {{inh|en|ang|sǣte|t=house}}, which is related to {{cog|goh|sāza|t=sedan, seat, domicile}}.

{{col-top|2|cog}}
* {{cog|dum|gesaete}}
* {{cog|goh|gisazi}} (modern {{cog|de|Gesäß}})
{{col-bottom}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/siːt/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-seat.ogg|a=US}}
* {{hyph|en|seat}}
* {{rhymes|en|iːt|s=1}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

[[File:1970 Jaguar XJ6 4.2 Series 1 - Flickr - The Car Spy (25).jpg|thumb|An automobile '''seat''']]

# Something to be sat upon.
## {{senseid|en|sitting place}} A [[place]] in which to sit.
##: {{ux|en|There are two hundred '''seats''' in this classroom.}}
##* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=VIII|passage=The humor of my proposition appealed more strongly to Miss Trevor than I had looked for, and from that time forward she became her old self again;{{nb...}}. Our table in the dining-room became again the abode of scintillating wit and caustic repartee, Farrar bracing up to his old standard, and the demand for '''seats''' in the vicinity rose to an animated competition.}}
##* {{quote-journal|en|year=2019|month=October|title=South Wales open access bid|journal=Modern Railways|page=15|text={{...}} Grand Union proposes making a '''seat''' part of the price of a ticket, with 50% refunds for those travelling for longer than 30 minutes unable to obtain a '''seat'''.}}
## The [[horizontal]] portion of a [[chair]] or other [[furniture]] designed for sitting.
##: {{ux|en|He sat on the arm of the chair rather than the '''seat''', which always annoyed his mother.}}
##: {{ux|en|the '''seat''' of a saddle}}
## {{senseid|en|sitting furniture}} A piece of furniture made for sitting, such as a [[chair]], [[stool]], or [[bench]]; any [[improvised]] place for sitting.
##: {{ux|en|She pulled the '''seat''' from under the table to allow him to sit down.}}
### {{senseid|en|ejection seat}} {{lb|en|aviation|military|slang}} An [[ejection seat]].
###: {{ux|en|Hey, fighter boy, our radar's putting out enough energy to launch your '''seat''' from this distance!}}
## {{senseid|en|buttocks}} The [[part]] of an object or individual (usually the [[buttock]]s) directly involved in sitting.
##: {{ux|en|Instead of saying "sit down", she said "place your '''seat''' on this chair".}}
## {{senseid|en|clothing}} The part of a piece of [[clothing]] (usually [[pants]] or [[trousers]]) covering the buttocks.
##: {{ux|en|The '''seat''' of these trousers is almost worn through.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1913|author={{w|Norman Lindsay}}|title={{w|A Curate in Bohemia (novel)|A Curate in Bohemia}}|publisher=N.S.W. Bookstall Co.|year_published=1932|location=Sydney|page=96|passage=Besides the broad-brimmed hat, he was distinguished by a spotted tie, a pair of seedy check trousers rather baggy in the '''seat''', and a cut-away coat, much too tight for him.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|format=comic|author=Tom Armstrong|title=Marvin|date=Jul 20 2006|passage=I love these new biker pants I bought!  There's padding in the '''seat''' to protect my rear end.}}
## {{senseid|en|resting place}} {{lb|en|engineering}} A part or surface on which another part or surface rests.
##: {{ux|en|The '''seat''' of the valve had become corroded.}}
# {{senseid|en|site}} A location or site.
## {{senseid|en|membership}} {{lb|en|figuratively}} A [[membership]] in an organization, particularly a representative body.
##: {{ux|en|Our neighbor has a '''seat''' at the stock exchange and in congress.}}
## {{senseid|en|governing location}} The [[location]] of a governing body.
##: {{ux|en|Washington D.C. is the '''seat''' of the U.S. government.}}
##: {{ux|en|White Plains is the county '''seat''' of Westchester.}}
##* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-08-03|volume=408|issue=8847|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/science-and-technology/21582495-computers-will-help-people-understand-brains-better-and-understanding-brains The machine of a new soul]|passage=But how the neurons are organised in these lobes and ganglia remains obscure. Yet this is the level of organisation that does the actual thinking—and is, presumably, the '''seat''' of consciousness.}}
## {{senseid|en|district}} {{lb|en|certain Commonwealth countries}} An [[electoral district]], especially for a national legislature.
## {{senseid|en|residence}} A temporary residence, such as a country home or a hunting lodge.
## {{senseid|en|site}} The place occupied by anything, or where any person, thing or quality is situated or resides; a [[site]].
##* {{RQ:King James Version|Revelation|2|13|passage=Where thou dwellest, even where Satan's '''seat''' is.}}
##* {{RQ:Bacon Essayes|chapter=Of Building|passage=He that builds a fair house upon an ill '''seat''' committeth himself to prison.}}
##* {{RQ:Macaulay Goldsmith|passage=a '''seat''' of plenty, content, and tranquillity}}
##* {{RQ:Gandhi Experiments|chapter=XVII|passage=I stopped taking the sweets and condiments I had got from home. The mind having taken a different turn, the fondness for condiments wore away, and I now relished the boiled spinach which in Richmond tasted insipid, cooked without condiments. Many such experiments taught me that the real '''seat''' of taste was not the tongue but the mind.}}
## {{senseid|en|departmental placement}} {{lb|en|law|E&W}} One of a [[series]] of [[departmental]] [[placement]]s [[give]]n to a [[trainee]] solicitor as part of their [[training]] [[contract]].
## {{senseid|en|Hungarian region}} {{lb|en|historical}} Any of several [[autonomous]] [[region]]s in the [[medieval]] [[Kingdom of Hungary]].
# {{senseid|en|fire}} The starting point of a [[fire]].
# {{senseid|en|horseback posture}} [[posture|Posture]], or way of sitting, on [[horseback]].
#* {{RQ:Eliot Daniel Deronda|chapter=III|passage=She had so good a '''seat''' and hand she might be trusted with any mount.}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To put an object into a place where it will rest; to fix; to set firm.
#: {{ux|en|Be sure to '''seat''' the gasket properly before attaching the cover.}}
#* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=VI|passage=From their foundations, loosening to and fro, / They plucked the '''seated''' hills.|year=1873}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=IV|passage=One morning I had been driven to the precarious refuge afforded by the steps of the inn, after rejecting offers from the Celebrity to join him in a variety of amusements. But even here I was not free from interruption, for he was '''seated''' on a horse-block below me, playing with a fox terrier.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To provide with a place to sit.
#: {{ux|en|This classroom '''seats''' two hundred students.}}
#: {{ux|en|The waiter '''seated''' us and asked what we would like to drink.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1712|author=w:John Arbuthnot|title=An Essay Concerning the Effects of Air on Human Bodies
|passage=The guests were no sooner '''seated''' but they entered into a warm debate.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1887|author=w:Elizabeth Cady Stanton|title=History of Woman Suffrage
|passage=He used to '''seat''' you on the piano and then, with vehement gestures and pirouettings, would argue the case. Not one word of the speech did you understand.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To request or direct one or more persons to sit.
#: {{ux|en|Please '''seat''' the audience after the anthem and then introduce the first speaker.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|legislature}} To recognize the standing of a person or persons by providing them with one or more seats which would allow them to participate fully in a meeting or session.
#: {{ux|en|Only half the delegates from the state were '''seated''' at the convention because the state held its primary too early.}}
#: {{ux|en|You have to be a member to be '''seated''' at the meeting. Guests are welcome to sit in the visitors section.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To assign the seats of.
#: {{ux|en|to '''seat''' a church}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To cause to occupy a post, site, or situation; to station; to establish; to fix; to settle.
#: {{ux|en|This valve isn't '''seat'''ing properly.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Richard 3|act=IV|scene=ii|passage=Thus high {{...}} is King Richard '''seated'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Raleigh War|passage=They had '''seated''' themselves in Nova Guiana.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete|intransitive}} To [[rest]]; to [[lie down]].
#* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|book=VI|canto=IX|passage=The folds, where sheepe at night doe '''seat'''.}}
# To settle; to plant with inhabitants.
#: {{ux|en|to '''seat''' a country}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To put a seat or bottom in.
#: {{ux|en|to '''seat''' a chair}}
